ranking.rationale: The hardest-to-fake magic is a fingertip flick that spins a tiny one-piece seed on a rounded belly, then a gravity-biased settle onto one face that ends in a knock. Pico Press owns compact support-free toys whose spin, roll, and wobble cycles are themselves the spectacle.
Bob owns Wish-specific kinetic machines, so a spinning settle is in his neighborhood, but this object is a one-piece fingertip tumbler rather than an exposed gear, cam, or crank machine.
The self-righting bias is a real physical phenomenon Ivy could teach, yet the Wish asks for a playable seed with a knock, not a science instrument or labeled demonstration.
The soft knock is acoustic, but it is only the landing of a spin-and-settle cycle. Sound is not the playable instrument.
Mira Fold owns compact two- or three-part tactile puzzles. This Wish is a one-piece motion toy, not a fit-together puzzle.
Vela Bloom owns deployable unfurling transformations. The seed does not blossom, iris, or unfold.
Kestrel Knot owns captive loops, braids, and continuous paths. This is a free tumbler, not a topology toy.
Tess Loop owns flat modular tessellations. A spinning seed is a single volumetric body, not a pattern set.
Luma Vale owns hand-powered light, aperture, and moiré effects. The Wish is tactile motion, not an optical transform.
Orin Shadow owns projected shadow stories. Nothing here is an occluder or hidden silhouette.
Alice personalizes known tabletop classics without changing their rules. This is not a classic game.
Leo invents original printable games with simulated opponents. The Wish is a single kinetic object, not a game.
Abstract Boardgame Oracle invents combinatorial board games. There is no board, piece set, or rule structure here.
Eve builds cinematic little worlds from a person's real references. The Wish names a generic spinning seed, not a private place or companion.
